mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months signals an active monetary easing cycle, reducing discount rates on future corporate earnings and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive in periods where FEDFUNDS declines, as measured by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero mean return.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in non-farm payroll growth above 200k signals strong labor market demand, which supports consumer spending and corporate revenue growth, driving positive S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX produces negative or flat 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where PAYEMS rises above 200k, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both residential investment (HOUST) and real personal consumption (RSAFS) indicates strong aggregate demand, which increases corporate earnings visibility and supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
failure_condition: The joint signal of rising HOUST and RSAFS fails to produce positive 60-day SPX returns in > 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a regression model has a coefficient with p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening real economic activity, which increases the risk of recession and triggers equity market sell-offs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below its 12-month moving average
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO drops below its 12-month MA, as confirmed by a t-test p-value > 0.05 against zero.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the CPIAUCSL above 2.5% year-over-year signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy, which increases real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods where CPIAUCSL exceeds 2.5% YoY, or the Rank IC over any 2-year window is not below -0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A contraction in real GDP (GDPC1) over the past quarter, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a weakening demand environment, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines in the prior quarter AND UNRATE rises > 0.2pp in the prior month
failure_condition: The joint signal of declining GDPC1 and rising UNRATE fails to predict negative 60-day SPX returns in > 50% of cases, or the interaction term in a predictive model has a p-value > 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market overheating condition—defined by a falling unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% and a payroll growth (PAYEMS) above 250k—signals tight labor supply, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to Fed tightening and negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5 AND PAYEMS > 250k in the prior month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE < 4.5 and PAYEMS > 250k, or the interaction effect has a p-value > 0.05 in a regression model.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0, combined with a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE), indicates a supply-side contraction and weakening demand, which reduces corporate profitability and triggers negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 105.0 AND UNRATE increases > 0.1pp in the prior month
failure_condition: The joint signal of INDPRO < 105.0 and rising UNRATE fails to produce negative 5-day SPX returns in > 60% of cases, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
